figures.finding: Gibraltar has no licence for child performers: the Employment Act's child (under fifteen) is barred only from industrial undertakings and ships (and, by regulations, shops), and persons under eighteen from the listed risky work, so performing work is not reached by an age bar.

barredFrom: shops (Shop Hours (Children and Young Persons) Regulations 1990)
value.reachesWritingDirecting: no age bar outside the named sectors

sources.said: “child” means a person under the age of fifteen years
No child shall be employed in any industrial undertaking
No child shall be employed in any ship.

figures.finding: In Gibraltar a child is anyone under eighteen; a child's contracts for money lent or for goods other than necessaries are void, but the Act leaves valid any contract a child may by law enter save those that are voidable (the common law of minors' contracts); no statute sets a child's earnings aside.

value.void: loans and goods other than necessaries
value.otherContracts: common law (beneficial contracts of service bind)

sources.said: “child” means a person who is under the age of 18

All contracts, whether by specialty or by simple contract, entered into by a child for the repayment of money lent or to be lent, or for goods supplied or to be supplied (other than contracts for necessaries), and all accounts stated with a child are absolutely void. (2) Nothing in this Act shall invalidate any contract into which a child may, by any law enter, except such as are voidable.
